title: Journal of Research High School (JRHS)
fee_timing_verbatim: 'a submission fee of $350 is required for all new manuscripts'
refundable: NOT STATED — the official FAQ is silent on refunds
acceptance_rate_official: 'Approximately, 30% of the submitted research papers have been published.'
expected_cost_per_publication: ~$1,167 (=$350 / 0.30) — arithmetic on the journal's OWN published acceptance rate, not an estimate of ours
eligibility_verbatim: 'Anyone who enrolls in high school or equivalent at the time of the initial submission is welcome'
rolling_verbatim: 'The journal publishes as a rolling base meaning your manuscript will be reviewed once it is submitted'
rolling_note: This IS an explicit official rolling statement, quoted verbatim — not inferred from absence of a deadline.
review_timeline: 'In general, the turnaround time is approximately 3 - 6 months'
recommendation: Do NOT surface as a 'research opportunity'. A student pays $350 up front against the journal's own stated ~70% rejection rate, with no stated refund. If retained at all it must be labelled a paid publication venue with the fee timing and acceptance rate shown together — showing $350 without the 30% is materially misleading.
unresolved: Refund policy on rejection is unstated by the journal — worth one direct email before any student is advised to pay.

title: International Journal of High School Research (IJHSR)
fee_timing_verbatim: 'A $350 publication fee will be requested only after an article has successfully completed the review process and has been accepted for publication.'
refundable: n/a — nothing is paid unless accepted
acceptance_rate_official: NOT STATED overall. For review articles only: 'IJHSR accepts only two or three review articles per issue; therefore, the selection process is extremely competitive.'
eligibility_verbatim: 'High school students and their mentors from any country may submit advanced research for consideration.'
eligibility_placement: Stated in the submissions section as the eligibility rule itself. Meets the placement test.
rolling_verbatim: 'There is no deadline for submission for any issue. IJHSR accepts submissions all year long without a deadline.'
publisher_note: Same organisation that runs GENIUS Olympiad, already in the corpus. Worth knowing when weighing independence.
recommendation: Still not a 'research opportunity' — it is where you send finished research. But its risk profile is completely different from JRHS's despite an identical $350 in the cost column: here a rejected student pays nothing. The corpus currently cannot express that difference, which is the real defect.

title: Journal of Emerging Investigators (JEI)
fee_verbatim: '$49 fee for each submission'; 'All submission fee payments are nonrefundable.'; 'paying the submission fee does not guarantee your manuscript will be published'
fee_history: Raised from $35 effective 2024-02-19 per the journal's own blog post.
waiver: Scholarships exist to cover the submission fee for students who cannot afford it; the FAQ points to the journal's giving/support page rather than stating criteria.
acceptance_rate_official: NOT STATED by JEI itself. (A 70-75% figure circulates in secondary/commercial blogs — NOT usable, no official source found.)
international_verbatim: 'YES! JEI takes submissions from outside of the United States. Anyone is welcome to submit to JEI that meets our author eligibility criteria.'
adult_submitter_rule_verbatim: 'Students are not allowed to submit their own work as we require there to be an adult outside of any 18+ student authors on each manuscript.'
adult_submitter_note: DECISION-RELEVANT: a student working entirely alone cannot submit here at all. They need an adult co-signer. This is a real blocker for unmentored students and is invisible in the current record.
review_process: Two-stage review; students receive written feedback from reviewers. Timeline explicitly varies: 'The length of the review process varies based on time of year, number of submissions...'
recommendation: Of the four paid venues this is the only one whose cost is not a barrier ($49, with waivers). Its `cost` is currently NULL in the DB while the $350/$496 journals have theirs filled in — so the corpus makes the cheapest option look like the unknown one. Also carries an eligibility blocker (adult submitter required) that is not recorded anywhere.

title: American Journal of Student Research (AJSR)
identity_check: CONFIRMED. Page self-identifies as 'American Journal of Student Research®', ISSN 2996-2218 — matches the stored title and the stored domain ajosr.org. Not a name-similarity match.
fee_verbatim: 'The current Article Processing Charge (APC) is $496'; 'An Article Processing Charge (APC) is required upon acceptance of an article'; 'payable only if the article is accepted for publication.'
refundable_verbatim: 'The Article Processing Charge (APC) and any other fees are non-refundable and may be subject to change.'
waiver_verbatim: 'APC reductions may be granted only in cases of genuine financial hardship.'; 'Authors requesting APC reductions may be asked to provide documentation of U.S. free or reduced-price lunch eligibility.'; 'Requests for APC reductions will not be considered once a manuscript has been accepted.'
waiver_trap_note: TWO decision-critical traps an advisor must surface BEFORE submission, not after: (a) the reduction must be requested BEFORE acceptance — a student who waits until the invoice arrives has permanently lost the option; (b) the named hardship documentation is US free/reduced-price lunch eligibility, which an international student simply does not have, so the waiver route is effectively US-shaped even though the journal accepts non-US authors.
who_may_submit_verbatim: 'An online, open-access academic journal dedicated to publishing scholarly work and research conducted by high school and undergraduate students'
recommendation: Not a research opportunity. Highest single fee of the four venues at $496. Fee-on-acceptance means no money is lost on rejection — but the waiver timing rule means the affordability decision must be made at submission time, which is precisely the moment the current record gives a student no information about.

title: Columbia Junior Science Journal (CJSJ)
severity: HIGH — live row is verified_current + cycle_status=open with a deadline 38 days out, and its official_url does not resolve
dns_evidence: `dig +short cjsjournal.org` returns no answer; `curl -L http://cjsjournal.org/` fails with 'Could not resolve host: cjsjournal.org' (exit 6). The `www.` variant resolves to 192.168.1.1, a private RFC1918 address — that is local resolver NXDOMAIN hijacking, not a real host. Both are dead.
correct_url_evidence: Resolves and serves the journal; self-identifies as 'The Columbia Junior Science Journal' run by Columbia University in partnership with the Columbia Undergraduate Science Journal (CUSJ).
deadline_note: The stored deadline is CORRECT and is 38 days from retrieval — this row is genuinely urgent, which makes the dead URL worse, not better: a student acting on a real deadline lands on nothing.
eligibility_verbatim: 'High school students from anywhere in the world are welcome to make their submission.'
graduate_exclusion_verbatim: 'we no longer accept submissions by high school graduates.'
graduate_exclusion_note: Decision-relevant for rising freshmen: a student who has just graduated is ineligible even if the research was done in high school.
eligibility_placement: Answer to the FAQ eligibility question — meets the placement test.
review_process_verbatim: 'you will receive progressive notifications on the status of your application in early November (semifinalists) and late December (finalists).'
recommendation: Fix official_url to columbiajuniorsciencejournal.org immediately — this is a one-field correction with real student impact and a hard deadline behind it. Separately: this exposes a systemic gap — evaluateRecommendationReadiness() checks that official_url EXISTS but never that it RESOLVES, so a dead link passes every hard blocker. Worth a corpus-wide URL liveness sweep.
unresolved: Whether CJSJ charges any fee is unstated on its own site — do not record 'free' until officially confirmed.
cycle_status_note: Matches the live row (verified_current/open) and its own published 2026-09-30 deadline, 37 days out at audit.
cost_note: No fee is stated on either the current live page (columbiajuniorsciencejournal.org) or its FAQ. Secondary sources claim CJSJ is free; that claim is NOT officially confirmed. Recorded as unknown, not free.

title: Pioneer Research Institute
proposed_category: research (KEEP — this one genuinely is a research programme)
commercial_flag: COMMERCIAL — run by Pioneer Academics, a private public-benefit corporation, not a university
cost_verbatim: 'Pioneer's tuition is 7,465 US dollars.'; '*Certain concentrations may require an additional fee no greater than 2% for laboratory equipment and materials.'
cost_note: Stored cost of $7,465 is CORRECT, but the possible +2% lab/materials surcharge is not represented anywhere.
financial_aid_verbatim: 'These funds are limited and restricted to cases in which the financial need of students' families can be reliably verified through partnering schools and non-profit organizations.'
financial_aid_note: DECISION-CRITICAL CONDITIONAL: aid is not need-based in the ordinary sense — it is gated on the student's school or an NGO being a Pioneer PARTNER able to verify need. A student from a non-partner school in Türkiye may have genuine need and still no route to aid. Never present this as 'financial aid available' without the partner condition.
acceptance_rate_official: 'On average, less than a third of applicants to the Research Institute are accepted.'
acceptance_rate_note: An official selectivity statement — rare and usable. Supports treating Pioneer as genuinely selective rather than pay-to-enter, which is the honest distinction from the commercial essay-prize tier.
eligibility_verbatim: 'High school students (9th-12th grade) from around the world demonstrating academic excellence, intellectual curiosity and a readiness for independent research are encouraged to apply.'; 'All applicants must demonstrate academic excellence and proficiency in English.'
college_credit_verbatim: 'Successful completion of the Pioneer Research Institute and achieving a grade of C-minus or higher earns a student four college credits — the maximum possible for a standard undergraduate course — awarded by Oberlin College and Conservatory.'
deadline_verbatim: 'The final deadline for Spring applications will be released in the 3rd week of October'; 'The final deadline for Summer applications will be released in the 2nd week of January'
deadline_note: Official statement that dates are announced later — an explicit 'not announced', NOT rolling. Two intakes per year.
sibling_programme_missing: Pioneer also runs the Global Problem-Solving Institute at $3,100 with 2 college credits from UNC Chapel Hill, grades 8-12, min 3.3 unweighted GPA. The corpus has only the $7,465 programme, so the cheaper sibling is invisible. Candidate new record.
recommendation: KEEP as research — it is a real, accredited, selective research programme. But it is the most expensive row in the corpus at $7,465 and CEO reports it currently matches all 7 test users at the same match_score as $0 programmes. The fix is representation (cost + aid conditionality reaching the recommendation surface), not removal.

title: Interlochen Review
proposed_category: WRONG CORPUS for 'research' — creative-writing/arts literary journal
identity_check: CONFIRMED via the stored URL itself (interlochenreview.org/submit).
disposition_verbatim: 'The Interlochen Review is an online literary journal produced by the creative writing students of Interlochen Arts Academy.'
what_it_publishes: Fiction (<5,000 words), poetry, nonfiction essays, hybrid genres, original songs, scripts/screenplays (<40 pages), visual arts. No scientific or scholarly research of any kind.
eligibility_verbatim: 'Talented high school writers, singer-songwriters and artists (grades 9-12 or high school postgraduate year) from around the world.'
cycle_status_evidence: 'Currently not open for submissions. Check back in January, 2027.'
recommendation: Remove from category='research'. It is a legitimate and genuinely worldwide opportunity — for a WRITER or ARTIST, not a researcher. Misfiled here it both pollutes research matching and hides itself from the students it would actually serve. Note the grade rule usefully includes a 'high school postgraduate year', which is broader than most.
note_for_ceo: This row alone shows the category problem is not cosmetic: a student whose weakest dimension is Research could be handed a poetry submission as the fix.
cost_note: No fee is stated on the pages retrieved (interlochenreview.org). Not confirmed free.

title: Research Science Institute (RSI)
proposed_category: research (KEEP — genuine, and among the most selective in the world)
organization: Center for Excellence in Education (CEE), held at MIT
cycle_status_verbatim: 'Applications for RSI 2026 are now closed. No late applications will be considered.'
deadline_note: Next-cycle (RSI 2027) dates not published as of retrieval. US applications historically open in the autumn; do NOT infer a date.
cohort_size_verbatim: 'Each summer, 100 of the world's most accomplished high school students gather at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) for the Research Science Institute (RSI).'
cost_verbatim: 'RSI is the first cost-free to students, summer science & engineering program to combine on-campus course work in scientific theory with off-campus work in science and technology research.'
grade_rule_verbatim: 'High school juniors are eligible. High school seniors are not.'; 'RSI participants have exceptionally strong academic ability and background and are about to enter their last year of high school. Typically, this means students apply in the middle of their junior year (a.k.a. third year, or grade 11) of high school.'
academic_bar_verbatim: 'It is recommended that PSAT Math Scores be at least 740 or higher and the Evidence-Based Reading and Writing Score be 700 or higher. ACT math scores should be at least 33 and verbal scores at least 34. Lower scores must be offset by strong indicators of mathematical, scientific, and academic potential...'
international_route_verbatim: 'There are two types of applications, U.S. Citizens/Permanent Residents and International Applicants.' — 'International Applicants: Each participating country has its own selection procedure and selection schedule. Please contact RSI to determine if your country participates. If it does, her team will put you in contact with the appropriate representative at the agency conducting selection for your country.'
international_route_note: DECISION-CRITICAL AND CURRENTLY UNRECORDED: an international student CANNOT apply to CEE directly. They must go through their own country's selecting agency, each with its own separate deadline. The list of participating countries is NOT published — CEE asks you to contact them. So for a non-US student the honest advice is 'contact RSI to find out whether your country participates', which is a completely different action from 'apply by date X'. Same national-member-organisation pattern oryn-ce documented for IPO/IYPT.
us_route_verbatim: 'All U.S. students, including U.S. Citizens studying overseas, with one year remaining before graduation from high school, may apply to RSI... Students are not nominated or selected by their schools.'
eligible_countries: US direct; other countries ONLY where a participating national agency exists — list unpublished
structure: One week of intensive STEM classes, then a five-week individual research internship under experienced scientist mentors, then a final week of written and oral presentations.
fetch_method: Browser pane (WebFetch received HTTP 403 from cee.org)
recommendation: Keep and promote to verified_current. This is the strongest genuine research row in the corpus: free, 100 places worldwide, real mentored research. Its record must carry the two-route eligibility structure or it will mislead every non-US student who sees it.
unresolved: Whether Türkiye is a participating country, and if so which agency selects — plausibly TÜBİTAK given its §7.1.2 role sending students to international competitions, but ASSERTED BY NOBODY OFFICIAL. Must be confirmed with CEE before telling any Turkish student this route exists.

title: STEM Fellowship Journal (SFJ)
identity_check: CONFIRMED — page self-identifies as 'STEM Fellowship Journal', ISSN 2369-0399, matching the stored domain journal.stemfellowship.org.
scope_verbatim: 'An open-access, peer-reviewed journal that is entirely dedicated to the original university and high school students' research in the STEM fields.'
scope_note: Publishes BOTH university and high-school student research — so a 15-year-old is competing for space against undergraduates. Relevant to expectations and invisible in the current record.

Authors pay an Open-Access publication fee only when their manuscript successfully passes peer review and reaches the final stages of publication.'
fee_amount: NOT STATED on the pages retrieved — author-guidelines page returned an error at retrieval time
fetch_method: Browser pane (WebFetch received HTTP 403; site is behind Cloudflare)

spinoff_candidate: SFJ publishes the 'National High School Big Data Challenge' run by STEM Fellowship with RBC, Let's Talk Science, Cisco Academy, National Research Council Canada and others — that is a genuine data-science research COMPETITION and is not in the corpus. Flagged for my competitions workstream.
unresolved: Whether SFJ is open to students outside Canada.

title: Georgetown Pre-College Online Program (Medicine / Journalism & Media)
proposed_category: WRONG CATEGORY — commercial taught online course, not research
severity: HIGH — second-worst undisclosed cost in the corpus after Pioneer
cost_gap_note: The live row stores NO cost at all for a $1,895 product. A student is shown a 'research opportunity' with the price field empty.
what_it_actually_is_verbatim: '100% online learning' via 'video lectures', 'engaging multimedia, simulations, and curated assignments'. The capstone asks students to 'design the ideal healthcare team' for a hypothetical patient scenario — applying taught concepts, NOT conducting original research.
credential_verbatim: Students 'Earn a Certificate of Completion from Georgetown University'
credential_note: A certificate of completion, explicitly NOT academic credit. Contrast Pioneer, which grants 4 real Oberlin College credits for $7,465. Georgetown Pre-College Online grants none for $1,895.
selectivity: No selection process stated — enrolment appears open to anyone who pays. This is the defining difference from Pioneer (<1/3 accepted) and RSI (100 places worldwide).
operator_note: Delivered via the third-party platform precollegeprograms.org under Georgetown branding; the page credits Georgetown faculty design. Worth flagging that the university brand is doing heavy lifting for what is a paid, non-selective, non-credit online course.
recommendation: Remove from research. If retained anywhere it must carry the $1,895 price, 'certificate only, no credit', and 'no selective admission'. Presenting this as research is the single clearest example of ORYN telling a student that paying money is a substitute for doing research.
deadline_note: NOT STATED on the official page — no application deadline published; enrolment appears open to anyone who pays.

title: Özyeğin University Summer Research Program (Lise Öğrencileri Yaz Staj Programı)
cost_verbatim: 'All of our summer research programs are free'; 'Participants can stay in dormitories free of charge during the program period. Lunch...will be covered by the university.'
cost_note: Stored cost of 0.00 is CORRECT, and understates the benefit: free dormitory accommodation and lunch are also provided — materially important for a student travelling from outside Istanbul.
eligibility_note: Unusually broad — no grade restriction, so a 14-year-old 9th grader is eligible. Rare among research programmes and worth surfacing.
eligible_countries: NOT STATED — the page carries no citizenship or residency rule either way. Must NOT be recorded as Türkiye-only by inference, nor as worldwide.
selection_verbatim: 'Students are chosen as a result of the evaluations done by the project owner academicians.'
cycle_status_conflict: CONFLICT TO FLAG, NOT SILENTLY RESOLVE. The official page banner reads 'APPLICATIONS FOR 2026 ARE NOW OPENED', but the live row is cycle_status='closed' with deadline 2026-05-15 (last verified 2026-08-23). Retrieval date is 2026-08-23 — a summer programme whose deadline was 15 May has already run this year, so the page banner is almost certainly stale rather than the DB being wrong. I am NOT flipping the row to open on the strength of a banner.
cycle_status_recommendation: Keep cycle_status='closed'. Re-check the page in spring 2027 for the next cycle. This is the mirror image of the stale-banner shape lib/opportunities/lifecycle.ts documents: here the SOURCE is stale-open while the DB is correctly closed.
recommendation: Keep in research. One of very few free, genuine, in-Türkiye research opportunities — directly relevant to ORYN's Turkey focus and complementary to TÜBİTAK 2204-A (CR1-002).
unresolved: Whether non-Turkish or overseas students may apply — unstated.

sip.ucsc.edu/admissions/index.html returned 404 — the correct admissions URL needs discovery.

title: STEM Enhancement in Earth Science (SEES) Summer Intern Program
organization: University of Texas at Austin, Center for Space Research (with NASA)
research_nature_verbatim: Students 'work beside NASA and other aerospace subject matter experts analyzing and visualizing data' and complete 'authentic NASA research through field investigations and data analysis'. They 'present their research during the Virtual SEES Science Symposium.'
grade_rule_note: The live row stores minimum_age=16 with no maximum. The official rule is grade-based (10th and 11th), which is not the same thing — a young 10th grader of 15 is eligible by grade but excluded by the stored age floor.
cost_verbatim: 'Housing, meals, and local transportation will be provided for those selected for scholarship and those fee-based students selected to attend. A limited number of travel scholarships to Texas may be available.'
cost_note: IMPORTANT AND UNRECORDED: the page distinguishes scholarship students from 'fee-based students', so there IS a paying route — but no fee amount is published. Stored cost is NULL, which reads as 'free'. It is not established as free.
eligible_countries_note: Citizenship/residency is NOT STATED on the page I retrieved. The stored 'United States' came from earlier research; I am neither confirming nor contradicting it without evidence.
recommendation: Keep in research. Two corrections worth making: replace the age floor with the grade rule (10th-11th), and record that a fee-based route exists so the null cost is not read as free.
